title: I'm in Love with the Older Girl Next Door
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Tasuku, a 13-year-old middle schooler, is in love with his neighbor Shia, a film-loving high-school girl three years older. They watch movies together every Wednesday, and each time he confesses she gently turns him down. The ANN reviewer reads it less as a romcom than a coming-of-age story about a boy learning self-awareness.
life_message: Growing up means learning to see yourself honestly and to respect another person's feelings, even when they don't match your own.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Tasuku freely pursues his feelings; Shia freely refuses.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Neighbour families and siblings present (MangaUpdates tags) but secondary.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Age gap gives Shia a mild senior role he tries to close by maturing.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: No religious frame; personal growth guides the story.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Shared film hobby and emotional honesty; low-stakes everyday life.

folkways.japan: The older-neighbour 'onee-san' figure and age-based seniority between middle and high schoolers reflect Japanese senpai-kohai norms.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewer says growth moments are rare and lessons are learned slowly through embarrassment.
delivery.note: Lessons about maturity are left for readers to infer from Tasuku's awkward attempts.

winners_losers: Tasuku gains self-awareness more than a girlfriend; Shia keeps her boundaries. Sympathy is shared between the earnest boy and the patient neighbour.
